ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done') · y gyt ac y + verb, 'as soon as' (y gyt ac y bedydywyt 'as soon as he was baptised'; y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'as soon as he came to the sea')
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall') · also (10) linking a fronted adjective to its noun, with soft mutation of the noun (ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'); here a is not the conjunction
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
chaer: Caer (Caer) — fortress; first part of Caer Aranrot (Caer Aranrhod), Aranrhod's court on the coast of Arfon; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'to' (parth a Chaer Aranrot 'towards Caer Aranrhod')
dathyl: Dathyl — second element of the place-name Kaer Dathyl, Math's court in Arfon (cf. Tathyl); radical
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also in e hun (ehun) 'self, own', unchanged for any person (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'; synnyaw e hun 'watching for himself') · also the y of y rof 'between me' in the oath (E rof a Duw 'between me and God') · also 'his' before a vowel and before h (e ystauell 'his chamber'; e hutlath 'his magic rod') · also the vocative particle a, written e (E porthawr 'O porter')
ymwelet: ymwelet (ymweld) — to visit; verbal noun (y ymwelet a mi 'to visit with me', i.e. to come and see me); no mutation
math: Math — personal name: Math son of Mathonwy, lord of Gwynedd (Math uab Mathonwy oed arglwyd ar Wyned 'Math son of Mathonwy was lord over Gwynedd'); radical here (soft form Uath is separate)
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God') · also soft as the object of welei (ef a welei uab bychan 'he saw a small boy'), after interrogative pa (Pa uab 'what son') and after possessive dy/y (dy uab 'your son', y uab 'his son')
mathonwy: Mathonwy — personal name, the father of Math (Math uab Mathonwy); genitive in a patronymic, no mutation
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that') · also (13) for predicative yn 'as', with soft mutation (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach) · (14) y ar 'from off' (y ar seith cantref Dyuet 'from off the seven cantrefs of Dyfed') · also y 'its, his' before a verbal noun, standing for the noun's object and softening it (na'y werthu 'nor selling it'; na'y ollwng 'nor releasing it') · y hediw 'from today' (a blwydyn y hediw 'and a year from today'); y 'to' before a verbal noun of purpose (lle idaw y benelinyaw 'a place for him to recline'); y 'his' twice in ar y bwyt a'y llynn 'on his food and his drink' · also (15) 'their' (for eu) with h- before a vowel (y harganuot o'r gaer 'their being seen from the fort'; a'y hanuon idi 'and sending them to her'), the h- being the possessive's sign
dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth) · also yd 'corn, grain' noun m. (y diua dy yd 'to destroy your corn')
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun · also 'it': the empty subject before a (Ef a dywetpwyt idaw 'it was said to him'; ef a allei llawer mab colli y eneit 'many a son might have lost his life') and 'it' of a thing (y medrwys y Lleu ef 'the fair one hit it', the wren)
tathyl: Tathyl — second element of Kaer Tathyl, Math's court, spelt Tathyl beside Dathyl; radical
troi: troi (troi) — to turn; verbal noun (Troi yn y hol a oruc ef 'he turned after her') · also 'to wrap, wind about' (guedy troi llenn o bali yn y gylch 'having wrapped a cloth of brocade about him')
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
wnaet: scribal slip for wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a (ymchwelut a wnaet 'he turned back')
hi: hi — 'she, her'; independent 3 sg. f. pronoun
glywei: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after a (ef a glywei llef erchwys arall 'he heard the cry of another pack')
lef: llef (llef) — cry, shout, blast; noun f., spelt lef, soft-mutated as the object of dot 'put' (dot lef 'give a cry')
corn: corn (corn) — horn; noun m. (corn canu 'a horn for blowing')
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying') · also 'into' with rithyaw (eu rithyaw yn llygot 'to change them into mice') · yn ol 'after' (yn ol guyr y Deheu 'after the men of the South'); yn + predicate with verbs of becoming, 'into, as' (yny uyd yn garw 'until he becomes a stag'; yn uab braswineu telediw 'into a boy'); yn y lle 'at once'; yn y taraw wynteu 'in their striking', striking them (y here for eu 'their', yn 'in')
ol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m. (yn ol y cwn 'after the hounds'; yn y ol 'in its track')
llef: llef (llef) — cry, voice; noun f. (llef yr erchwys 'the cry of the pack')
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
mynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun (amser mynet y uwyta 'time to go to eat')
heibaw: heibaw (heibio) — past, by; adverb (athoed hi heibaw 'she had gone past')
cwn: ci (ci) — dogs; noun pl. of ci, the pack as individual animals (as against erchwys, the pack as a body)
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
wyr: gwyr (gwŷr) — men; noun pl., soft-mutated after yn (yn wyr ymi 'as men to me') · also soft after o 'of' (o wyr 'of men') and in address (A wyr 'O men') · also soft after y 'to' (y wyr Dyuet 'to the men of Dyfed') and y 'his' (y wyr 'his men')
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec) · also 'concerning, about', where am would be expected (ac ar Yspydaut Benn 'and concerning the Hospitality of the Head'; the Red Book also ar) · ar + verbal noun, 'to, in order to' (doethwyf i ar diuetha y pryf 'I have come to destroy the creature')
traet: troed (troed) — foot; noun, plural traet (traed) 'feet' (erwyd y traet 'by the feet'); radical after the article y
dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
was: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant; noun m., soft-mutated in address (Ha was 'ho, lad'; Bid parawt … was 'be ready, lad') and after wrth (wrth was y uarch 'to his groom', literally 'the lad of his horse') · also soft after predicative yn (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay') · also standing without its subject (Och, heb, pa ryw dygyuor 'alas, said (she), what kind of muster')
wybot: gwybot (gwybod) — knowledge, discernment; noun m. used substantively (ny bu gystal dy wybot 'your judgement was never so good') · also the verbal noun 'to know, find out', soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wybot pwy yw 'to find out who she is') · also after heb 'without' (heb wybot dim y wrthunt 'without knowing anything of them')
pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you') · also interrogative adjective 'what' before a noun (Pwy enw dy uab dy? 'what name has your son?'), no mutation
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness') · also the article before hwnn, honn, 'the one' (yr hwnn y tu a Chernyw 'the one on the side towards Cornwall'; yr honn a uu tryded anuat paluawt 'the one that was the third unfortunate blow') · also yr (er) 'for all' before the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'for all the grief they had seen') · also the article before a consonant in kyrchu yr gaer 'making for the fort' (read as the article, as the second witness takes it) · yr pan 'since' (yr pan welsei ef 'since he had seen'); the verb after it is soft-mutated
yniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host; noun m. with prosthetic y- (yr yniuer y buam doe 'the company that we were yesterday')
guas: guas (gwas) — lad, young man, servant; noun m. (guas ditheu 'a lad, you')
gouyn: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 2 sg. imperative 'ask!' (Gouyn ueithon y Wawl weicheu 'ask Gwawl for sureties') · also verbal noun 'asking', g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ouyn 'without asking') and after y 'to' (y ouyn idaw 'to ask of him'); also in a gouyn a wnaeth 'asking he did'
oedynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. imperfect 'they were' (nit oedynt unllef)
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
hwnn: hwnn (hwn) — 'this' (m.); demonstrative (yr oet hwnn 'this appointment') · also pronoun 'the one that' (namyn yr hwnn a dyly 'but that which it deserves') · also adjective 'this' after its noun (Y mab hwnn 'this boy')
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they') · also emphatic 'them' after a conjugated preposition (ganthunt wy 'from them', ohonunt wy 'of them') · also 'them' as object, resuming the infixed -s (bei as caffwnn i wy oll 'if I were to get them all') · also a spelling of uy 'my' (wy gwreic i 'my wife'; the nasal mutation is not written)
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that') · also adjective 'those' after its noun (a'r tri hynny 'and those three'); yn hynny 'in that (time), meanwhile' (Ac yn hynny ny doethant wy 'meanwhile they did not come')
dywot: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. preterite 'said' (irregular stem dywot beside dywedwys) (a dywot ef 'and he said')
idi: idi (iddi) — to her; 3 sg. f. conjugated form of y 'to' (menegi... a wnaeth idi)
hitheu: hitheu (hithau) — conjunctive form of hi 'she', 'she for her part'
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
gerdwys: kerdet (cerdded) — to go, walk; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (ef a gerdwys 'he went')
auon: afon (afon) — river; noun f. (dwy auon 'two rivers'); no mutation (vowel)
lad: lladd (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun (am lad o honaf uu hun uy mab 'for my killing of my own son'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition am · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive 'e 'his' (na'e lad 'nor his killing')
wrth: wrth (wrth) — to, towards, according to; preposition, base form (dywedut... wrthaw) · also 'at' (wrth y danned 'at the teeth'; wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone') and 'because of' (wrth hynny 'for that reason') · also 'with, over' (yn ymhalogi wrth y pryf hwnnw 'defiling yourself with that creature'); in ac wrth y llinyn 'and by the cord' the sense is uncertain
llithyaw: llithyaw (llithio) — to feed hounds on a kill, the huntsman's reward after a hunt; verbal noun
gwn: ci (ci) — dog; plural cwn, soft-mutated c > g after e 'his' (e gwn 'his dogs') · also gwybot (gwybod) 'to know'; 1 sg. present 'I know' (Gwn, Arglwyd 'I know, Lord'), radical form, repeating the verb of the question
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them') · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny uu damunet gantunt 'until there was desire in them') and as after the relative a left unwritten (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man') · also 'she was' after a fronted predicate, the relative a understood (a lleidyr uu hi arnaf i 'and a thief she was against me') · also an apparent slip for uy (fy) 'my' in mi uu hun 'I myself' (the Red Book has miui uy hun)
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
phan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A phan doeth yno) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no phan uuassei 'than when he had been')
atueilaw: atueilaw (adfeilio) — to decay, waste away; verbal noun (yn atueilaw 'wasting away', said of his colour and looks); no mutation (vowel)
nessau: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; verbal noun (yn nessau yn ebrwyd attunt 'drawing near swiftly to them'); no mutation
doeth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (a doeth 'and came')
porth: porth (porth) — gate, gateway, entrance; noun m. (y porth 'the gate'); no mutation
dioer: dioer — assuredly, indeed; an oath, a worn-down Duw a wyr 'God knows'
ni: ni — (1) 1 pl. pronoun 'we/us' (yd ymdidanyssam ni); (2) negative particle, spelling variant of ny before some verbs (ni ladaf, ni bu) · also a scribal slip here for the emphatic i (Ny wnn ni amgen no'm bot 'I know no other than that I am (a maiden)'); the n of wnn written twice
gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many') · also 'beside, along' (gan lann y weilgi 'along the shore of the sea'; gan pob llong 'for every ship, by reason of the ships')
unben: unben (unben) — chieftain, lord; noun m., un 'one' + penn 'head'; vocative form of address · also 'the chieftain' as an ordinary noun (gan yr unben 'in the mind of the chieftain')
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another') · also 'again, more' after kymeint (y gymeint arall 'as much again')
onys: ony (oni) + 's 'it' — unless, if not (onys gwyr 'unless she knows it'); ony with infixed object pronoun s
arglwydes: arglwydes (arglwyddes) — lady; feminine of arglwyd, term of address
kennadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger; plural kennadeu 'messengers' (cenhadon); no mutation (subject, radical: Sef kennadeu a aeth 'the messengers who went')
erbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — (1) against, by (a time) (erbyn hanner dyd 'by midday'); (2) 'to meet' (yn y erbyn 'to meet him')
kymerth: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; old 3 sg. preterite without -wys ending (y kymerth ynteu y furuf e hun)
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
graessawu: graessawu (croesawu) — to welcome; verbal noun (a'y graessawu 'and welcoming them'); g- is the word's own initial in this spelling, as in grayssaw, not a mutation
gyuarch: kyuarch (cyfarch) — to greet; verbal noun (y gyuarch guell idaw 'to greet him', lit. 'to ask better to him'); soft-mutated (k>g) after y 'to'
well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land') · also soft as the predicate straight after the verb (nat oed well genti 'it was no better to her') · also na well 'no, not better', reply 'Na well' (soft-mutated gw>w after na) · also 'the better' with henbydy (ni henbydy well di 'you will not fare better'); soft after the verb, as a complement
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
dalho: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) repay' (Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you'), written with h before the ending (008 has dalo); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
dy: dy — 'your' (sg.); possessive pronoun, causes soft mutation (dy gerennyd 'your friendship') · also written for the affixed pronoun di 'you' after the presentative wely (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son')
lywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (diruawr lywenyd 'huge gladness'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preceding adjective diruawr · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive y 'his' (a dwyn y lywenyd y gantaw 'and taking his joy from him')
eisted: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; verbal noun (eisted a wnaethant 'they sat')
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
blodeued: Blodeued (Blodeuedd) — personal name, the woman made of flowers for Lleu, from blodeu 'flowers' (Red Book blodeuwed); radical, object of dodi (dodi Blodeued arnei 'putting Blodeuedd on her', naming her)
edrych: edrych (edrych) — to look; verbal noun (edrych ar y carw 'to look at the stag') · also imperative 'look!' (Edrych i'th gylch 'look around you') and 3 sg. present (A phan edrych 'and when he looked', the bare stem as vivid present; the Red Book a phan edrychawd ef)
awr: awr (awr) — hour; noun f. (hyt yr awr hon 'until this hour'); no mutation (vowel)
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
gyueir: kyueir (cyweir) — ready, equipped, in harness; adjective (ual y maent yn gyueir 'as they are, equipped'); soft-mutated (k>g) after predicative yn
arnei: ar — conjugated preposition 'on her' (a charyat arnei 'and love on her') · also 'on it', of a feminine noun (a eistedo arnei 'who may sit on it', of the mound)
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
llawn: llawn (llawn) — full; adjective (a uyd llawn dy got ti uyth 'will your bag ever be full?')
garyat: karyat (cariad) — love; noun m., soft-mutated after 'th 'your' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you') · also soft after gan 'with' (gan garyat a llywenyd 'with love and joy')
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
medwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m. (yn y uryt ac yn y uedwl)
yndaw: yn (yn) + ef — conjugated preposition 'in him' (angheuawl dyrnawt yndaw ynteu; yssyd yndaw ef)
yndi: yn (yn) + hi — conjugated preposition 'in her/it', feminine (Nit oes yndi nep; y guassanaeth yndi)
allwys: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. preterite 'could' in -wys (yny allwys marchogaeth pob march 'until he could ride every horse'); g lost by soft mutation after yny 'until'
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing') · also soft after dy 'your' (dy uot yn kyuanhedu 'your being settled')
charu: caru (caru) — to love; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her' (a'y charu 'and (to) love her')
gymerth: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 sg. preterite 'took', soft-mutated after a (Y march a gymerth 'he took the horse'; a gymerth rygyng 'took an amble')
diruawr: diruawr (dirfawr) — immense, vast, exceeding; adjective (diruawr llywenyd 'immense joy'); no mutation
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why') · also in o achaws 'because of' (o achaws y carchar hwnnw 'because of that prison')
pob: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective (pob un 'each one')
honunt: o — conjugated preposition 'of/from them', truncated (o honunt 'of them')
gilyd: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; variant spelling of gilid (ar y gilyd 'against the other') · also pwy gilyd 'each (to) the other, one another' (o'r pryt pwy gilyd), soft-mutated after pwy; sense of pwy here uncertain
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
eu: eu — 'their'; possessive pronoun (eu clusteu 'their ears') · also 'them' (object) before a verbal noun (ar hynny eu taraw a'r hutlath 'and thereupon striking them with the wand'; eu kyweiraw 'dressing them')
hymdidan: ymdidan — conversation, to converse; verbal noun/noun; h-prefix after y 'her' before a vowel-initial word (a'y hymdidan 'her conversation')
ohir: gohir (gohir) — delay, tarrying; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ohir 'without delay')
ymgael: ymgael (ymgael) — to meet, encounter (with a); verbal noun, takes a/ac (ymordiwes ac ef... ymgael a'r gwr)
amgen: amgen — other, different; adjective/adverb ('beth amgen' 'what else?'; 'amgen noc' 'other than')
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach) · also in kyn no hynny 'before that, earlier than that'
kyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, base form (yd wyt yn kyscu heno 'you are to sleep tonight')
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them') · y gyt ac y + verb 'as soon as' (y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'as soon as he came to the sea'); y gyt without a, 'together, as one' (ywch gerdet y gyt 'you to go together'); y gyt a chwi 'with you'
thrannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thrannoeth) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no thrannoeth 'than the next day')
arouun: arouun (arofun) — to intend, set out, make for; verbal noun (arouun y longeu a wnaeth ef 'he set out for his ships'); no mutation (vowel)
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
ey: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 sg. present/future 'you will go' (nyt ey idi 'you will not go into it'), the suppletive stem e-; no mutation after the negative nyt
wrthyf: wrth (wrth) + i — conjugated preposition 'to/at me' (na dywedy di wrthyf i)
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you') · also echoing a possessive (wy gwreic i yw hi 'she is my wife') · also for ni 'we' after a verb ending in -n, the n of the pronoun absorbed (A pha beth a wnawn i? 'and what shall we do?'; the Red Book a wnawn ni)
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
heuyt: heuyt (hefyd) — also, either; adverb (Ni wydwn achos it heuyt 'I did not know a reason for you either')
ganthunt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with them' (ni bu newydach ganthunt 'it was no more novel to them')
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
yg: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yg before a g: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg gwyd = yng ngwyd 'in the presence of'; yg got = yng nghod 'in a bag', with c>ngh after yn 'in') · also before k-: yg kylch y ty 'around the house' (yng nghylch), the g being the trace of the nasal mutation (c>ngh)
kyt: kyt (cyd) — although; conjunction, takes the subjunctive (kyt bwyf i yno)
oes: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. existential 'there is' (Nit oes yndi nep) · also oes 'age, lifetime, generation', noun f. (yn yr oes honno 'in that age')
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel') · also soft-mutated after nyt oes in (nyt oes in gynghor 'we have no counsel')
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me') · also 'except, but' (un dyn yma onyt pedwar dyn 'one man here except four men')
keissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun (keissaw dy welet ti 'seeking to see you')
ganthaw: gan — conjugated preposition 'with him' (y bu digrif ganthaw 'it was pleasant with him') · also in y ganthaw 'from him' (kymer gedernit y ganthaw 'take a pledge from him')
gwybot: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; verbal noun (ef yn gwybot y uot yn uab 'he knowing that he was a son'); no mutation
del: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may come' (a del yn waredauc 'whoever comes submissively')
angheu: angheu (angau) — death; noun m. (uy angheu i 'my death'; teruynedic angheu 'death is determined')
rith: rith (rhith) — shape, form, guise; noun m. (byd di i'm rith yno 'be there in my shape')
amdanaw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.); clothing/objects are 'about' a person (gwisc ... amdanaw)
trannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, base form
hediw: heddiw (heddiw) — today; adverb (na ommed neb hediw 'let no one be refused today')
uynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun, soft-mutated after e/y (e uynet e gyscu 'to go to sleep') · also softened as the object of a finite verb with other words between (Ni chymellaf inheu ar neb uynet 'I will not compel anyone to go')
canys: canys — since, for, because; conjunction (canys dechreueist uy llad 'since you have begun to kill me') · also for kan 'since' + nys 'not … it' (Canys collyghy yr hynny 'since you will not release it for that'; the Red Book Kan nys gellyngy) · also plain affirmative 'since' (A chanys bu 'and since she was')
ditheu: ditheu (dithau) — conjunctive form of ti 'you' (sg.), 'you for your part'
af: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 sg. present/future 'I go, I will go' (a af 'will go')
inheu: inheu (innau) — I/mine, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun marking contrast (a'm kyuoeth inheu 'my realm, mine') · also for ninheu 'we for our part', the n lost after a verb ending in -n (keisswn inheu 'let us try, we for our part'; the Red Book ninneu)
dywedaf: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; 1 sg. present 'I say' (Dywedaf wrthyt 'I say to you')
hagen: hagen (hagen) — however; adverb (Yr a rodwn i idau ef hagen 'however many I gave him')
bieu: piau (piau) — to own, be the owner of; 3 sg. present 'owns' (ef bieu y llongeu 'he owns the ships'); soft-mutated (p>b) in the relative construction after the fronted subject ef
ie: ie — yes; particle of assent, taking up what was just said
auory: auory (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (o'r dyd auory 'from the day tomorrow')
mi: mi — 1 sg. independent/emphatic pronoun 'I' (mi a wnn 'I know')
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
di: di — 'you' (sg.), echoing pronoun after a verb or possessive (y pryny di; dy gerennyd di); also the object 'you' (ni ladaf i di)
dywedeis: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 1 sg. preterite 'I said, have said' (na dywedeis 'that I have not said')
wrthyt: wrth (wrth) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to/at you' (Dywedaf wrthyt; chadw kywirdeb wrthyt titheu)
ymdidan: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, to converse; noun/verbal noun, base form (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth ef)
lut: glut (glud) — tenacious, persistent; adjective (amouyn yn lut 'asking persistently'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after adverbial yn; rare, meaning uncertain
dilyt: dilyt (dilyn) — to follow, pursue, keep on with; verbal noun (no dilyt kyuedach 'than to pursue carousing'); no mutation
gantaw: gan (gan) — 'with him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt gantaw (hyspys oed gantaw 'it was known to him'); no mutation
ford: ford (ffordd) — road, way; noun f., f written for ff (y'r ford 'to the road'; yr un ford 'the same way')
gallei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he could' (ual y gallei gyntaf 'as fast as he could')
enteu: ynteu (yntau) — he for his part; conjunctive 3 sg. m. pronoun, here spelt enteu (Enteu Math a gyrchwys 'and Math, for his part, made for'); no mutation
treulaw: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); verbal noun, base form
drwy: trwy (trwy) — through; preposition, soft-mutated form (drwy y dewred ef 'through his valour')
cherd: cerdd (cerdd) — song, music, minstrelsy; noun f.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a cherd a chyuedach 'and song and carousing')
chyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing, a drinking-feast; noun m., spirant-mutated after a (a chyuedach 'and carousing')
gyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y (y gyscu 'to sleep')
aethant: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. preterite 'they went' (yd aethant 'they went')
eil: eil (ail) — second; ordinal numeral (yr eil 'the second') · also in the name Dylan Eil Ton, eil 'second' or 'son, offspring' (sense of the epithet disputed)
wrthi: wrth (wrth) + hi — conjugated preposition 'to/at her' (ny dywot ef wrthi hi)
nis: ny (ni) + 's — negative particle with infixed 3 sg. f. object pronoun 'not her' (nis gordiwedut ti 'you would not overtake her'); a spelling variant beside nys; no mutation
cauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find; 3 sg. preterite 'found' (Sef lle y cauas Uendigeiduran 'the place where it [the bird] found Bendigeidfran'); radical after the particle y
derw: daruot (darfod) — to happen; derw = deryw, the old 3 sg. perfect 'it has happened' (a chan derw yt dywedut 'and since it has befallen you to say'); the Red Book also writes derw · also 'has ended, is done' (A derw … wiscaw amdan y gwryanc hwnnw? 'is the arming of that young man done?'), answered Deryw
yti: y (i) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to you', variant spelling (pa furyf y caf i dy gerennyd di... yti)
wyt: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
iach: iach (iach) — healthy, well; adjective (yn iach 'in health')
medylyaw: medylyaw (meddwl/myfyrio) — to think, ponder; verbal noun (medylyaw a wnaeth yn hir)
wyf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. present 'I am' (Brenhin corunawc wyf i)
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs') · also yr hynn 'that which, what' (yr hynn a deryw ymi 'what befalls me')
amdanaf: am — conjugated preposition 'about me'; Amdanaf innheu 'as for me, for my part' (1 sg.)
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one') · also 'because' before na (am na'th elwir y uorwyn 'because you are not called the maiden') and 'on account of' (am y dygyuor a bereisti 'on account of the muster you caused')
ot: ot (o + -t) — 'if' in the idiom ot gwnn 'if I know' = as far as I know, I trust · also 'if' before a vowel (ot oed uawr ef 'if he was big')
gynt: kynt (cynt) — (1) 'swifter', comparative of buan 'swift', softened after a noun (warch gynt 'a swifter horse'); (2) 'before, formerly', the softened adverb, modern gynt (no'r dyd gynt 'than the day before')
miui: mi (mi) — I/me; emphatic 1 sg. pronoun, fuller spelling of mi (A miui a af)
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise') · also with soft mutation of g (ony wybydaf i 'if I do not find out') · also 'if not' with the subjunctive (ony bei hagyr 'if it were not unseemly')
m: 'm — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'm, y'm, o'm etc.: 'my' (possessive, triggers soft mutation) or 'me' (object) · with h- before a following vowel (o'm hanwod 'against my will'); as 'my' before a verbal noun it may stand for that noun's object (a'm rodi 'and my giving' = and giving me); as 'me' after a relative (a'm gwrthyt 'who rejects me')
llad: llad (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun, base form (y'm llad i 'to kill me') · also llad glwm 'to tie a knot' (idiomatic, literally 'strike a knot'): llad glwm ar garryeu y got 'to tie a knot on the straps of the bag'
hawd: hawd (hawdd) — easy; adjective (nat hawd genhyf i 'it is not easy with me'); no mutation (h-)
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
wney: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present/future in -i (wnei) 'you do, you will do' (A wney ditheu gynghor arall? 'will you do another counsel?'; Iawn a wney 'you do right'); g lost by soft mutation after the particle a (interrogative, relative)
yrof: yr (er) + i — conjugated preposition 'for me' (A wnaethost, heb ef, yrof i)
menegi: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate; verbal noun (menegi y holl gyfranc a wnaeth idi)
ymi: y (i) + mi — conjugated preposition 'to me' (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi)
ba: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, a variant spelling with b (Ba ryw leidyr 'what kind of thief'; cf. byhyt for py hyt); whether b is a mutation here is uncertain; causes soft mutation of a following noun
guell: guell (gwell) — better; comparative adjective, in kyuarch guell 'greet' (literally 'ask better') · also the plain comparative 'better' (guell eu kic no chic eidon 'their flesh is better than beef'; ae guell 'is it better')
teu: teu (tau) — yours; independent possessive pronoun 2 sg., with the article (y teu di 'yours'), di echoing; no mutation
ergyt: ergyd (ergyd) — blow, stroke, shot; noun (a'r ergyt y doeth y angheu ohonaw 'and the blow by which his death came from him'; trydyd anuat ergyt 'the third ill-fated blow', one of three); radical; gender uncertain (f. in later Welsh)
reit: reit (rhaid) — need, necessity; noun m./f. (reit ymi 'need to me' = 'I need')
blwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f. (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end')
gwneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun/infinitive, also used as the periphrastic auxiliary 'do' (a wneuthum itt 'that I did to you')
par: peri (peri) — to cause, command, have done; 2 sg. imperative 'cause!, have!' (par wahard 'have forbidden')
dim: dim — anything, nothing; indefinite pronoun (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct before you')
honaw: o — conjugated preposition 'of/by him', written apart (gwledychu o honaw 'ruling by him'; o honaw 'by it')
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
pan: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction with a past-time clause (pan doeth) · also interrogative 'from where, whence' (pan doy di? 'where do you come from?') · also 'from where' as a relative (Pan doaf o Loygyr 'from where I come, from England')
ae: ae (ae) — either … or; correlative conjunction (ae a'e droet ae a throssawl 'either with his foot or with a staff'); no mutation · also interrogative particle 'is it that…?' (ae guell y gwna neb uy neges i wrthyt ti 'is it better that anyone does my errand to you…?')
ellir: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal present 'one can' (Peth a ellir wrth hynny? 'what can be done about that?'), -ir, a>e by affection; soft-mutated (g>∅) after the relative a · also softened after cany 'since not' (cany ellir 'since it cannot be done')
mywn: y mywn (i mewn) — in, inside; adverbial phrase (yn dyuot y mywn 'coming in') · also prepositional 'in' (y mywn gogof 'in a cave')
ty: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m. (yn y ty yd oed cassec 'in the house was a mare'); no mutation · also 'you', emphatic 2 sg. pronoun after the verb (yd wyt ty yndaw 'you are in it')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
uarch: march (march) — horse; noun m., soft-mutated after ar (y ar uarch erchlas mawr 'on a big dapple-grey horse') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uarch 'his horse') · also soft after o 'of' (a wely o uarch 'whatever you see of horses')
uyn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (A uyn ef dyuot y'r tir 'does he want to come ashore?'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the interrogative particle a · also uy (fy) 'my', with the nasal mutation of d- written as n on the possessive (uyn diua i 'my destruction') · also before teulu (uyn teulu 'my warband'), the n of the nasal mutation being written on the possessive · also uy (fy) 'my' before t- (Nit drwc uyn trawscwyd i 'my venture is not bad'), the n being the written trace of the nasal mutation; before deudecuet (ar uyn deudecuet 'with me as the twelfth')
troet: troed (troed) — foot; noun m., singular (yn y troet 'in the foot'); radical after the article y · also after uyn 'my', the nasal mutation written only on the possessive and troet left plain (uessur uyn troet 'the measure of my foot')
delw: delw (delw) — image, form, manner; noun f. (Pa delw 'in what manner')
ennein: ennein (ennaint) — bath; also ointment; noun m. (ennein yssyd reit ymi 'I need a bath')
im: im (i mi) — to me; conjugated preposition, contracted spelling (Meuyl im 'shame to me')
lan: glan (glan) — bank, shore; noun f., soft-mutated (g lost) after ar 'on' (ar lan y weilgi 'on the shore of the sea')
uch: uch (uwch) — above, over; preposition (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also 'high' as adjective/adverb, comparative in yn uch no bwrd y llong 'higher than the ship's board'
benn: penn (pen) — head, top, end; noun m.; soft-mutated (p>b) after ar 'on' (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'; ar benn y pethewnos 'at the end of the fortnight') · also soft after y 'his' (gauas y benn 'found his head') and after am 'about' (am benn hwnnw 'about that one's head') · also soft after a preceding adjective (Yspydawt Urdaul Benn 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head') and after the feminine noun yspydawt (Yspydaut Benn 'the Hospitality of the Head') · also soft-mutated (p>b) after uch 'above' (uch benn llech 'above a slab') · also soft after dy 'your' (am dy benn 'about your head')
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
dwyn: dwyn (dwyn) — to carry, bring; verbal noun (dwyn y dwy dyrnas yn un 'bringing the two kingdoms into one') · also 'to pass, spend, experience' a time (dwyn yspeit digriuach 'to pass a merrier time'); sense from context
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
gyr: ger (ger) — near, beside; preposition, spelt gyr (gyr y bron 'beside her breast'; gyr llaw hwnnw 'beside that'); no mutation
llaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., in the idiom uch llaw 'above, overlooking' (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also gyr llaw 'beside, next to' (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw 'to sit beside it') · also 'hand' without mutation after the article y (yn y llaw arall 'in the other hand') · also first element of the compound llaw gist 'hand-chest', a small chest (ymywn llaw gist 'inside a small chest') · also in the epithet Llaw Gyffes 'steady hand' (ys llaw gyffes 'it is with a steady hand'; Llew Llaw Gyffes), radical
neill: neill (naill) — one (of two); (o'r neill parth 'on the one side')
geuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y geuyn attei 'and his back to her') · also keuyn 'ridge' in the place-name y Geuyn Clutno, Cefn Clydno, softened after the preposition y 'to, of' (not the article, after which the masculine keuyn would not soften)
llall: llall (llall) — the other; pronoun, used with the article (y llall 'the other'); no mutation (subject)
bynnac: bynnac (bynnag) — -ever, indefinite particle after peth/pwy etc.; 'Peth bynnac' 'whatever'
yuelly: yuelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, the particle y fused with uelly (a chyt kerych di uot yuelly 'though you wish it to be so'; Ac yuelly y gwnaethpwyt 'and so it was done'); no mutation
wnay: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. imperfect 'would do, was to do', spelt -ay for -ei (na wydat beth a wnay ymdanei 'that he did not know what he should do about her'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour') · also 'from' after verbs of saving (waret rac hynn 'to deliver from this') · also 'because of, against' (chwynaw yn luttaf rac Aranrot 'complaining bitterly about Aranrhod')
dianc: dianc (dianc) — to flee, escape; verbal noun (kyt mynhei dianc 'though he wished to escape'); radical
kynt: kynt (cynt) — sooner, faster; comparative of buan 'swift' (nyt kynt … noc … 'no sooner … than'); also 'before, formerly'
noc: no (na) — than; spelling before a vowel (noc a uu 'than what was')
ymadrawd: ymadrawd (ymadrodd) — speech, utterance, talk; noun m. (yr ymadrawd hwnnw 'that speech'); no mutation (vowel)
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
gueith: gweith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, the thing made; noun m., gu- spells gw- (o'r gueith hwnnw 'of that work'; y gueith wynteu 'their work'); radical after the article and after y standing for eu 'their'
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
penn: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., base form (Penn Annwuyn 'Head of Annwfn')
ulwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., soft-mutated after y/the feminine article (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn) · also adverbial, 'a year' in time phrases, soft-mutated without the article (ulwydyn y heno 'a year from tonight'; ual yd eistedyssant ulwydyn o'r nos honno 'as they sat a year from that night'), the soft mutation being that of an adverbial accusative of time · also soft after a preceding ordinal (y seithuet ulwydyn 'the seventh year')
barawt: parawt (parod) — ready; adjective, soft-mutated after predicative yn (yn barawt 'ready') · also soft after the feminine noun cad (cad barawt 'ready for battle')
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
peris: peri (peri) — to cause, command; 3 sg. preterite 'he caused' (y peris ef dyuot 'he had come'); radical after the particle y
dywedeisti: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. preterite 'you said' in -eisti (-eist + i) (wrth a dywedeisti 'by what you said'); relative a 'what', so the soft mutation of d (>dd) is not visible
enneint: enneint (ennaint) — bath, bathing (the Middle Welsh sense; later 'ointment'); noun m. (Perwch enneint y'r gwyr 'have a bath made ready for the men'); no mutation, object of perwch
dangossaf: dangos (dangos) — to show, offer; 1 sg. present/future 'I will show' (Auory minheu a dangossaf gyfnewit 'tomorrow I for my part will show an exchange'); the soft form after a is not shown in the spelling
bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...') · also introducing a reported fact, 'that (it) was' (adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu 'knowing that their gain was failing'; clybot bot y gwyr 'hearing that the men were')
brynn: bryn (bryn) — hill; noun m., spelt brynn; first part of the hill-name Brynn Aryen, Bryn Arien; radical after a 'to'
elwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (y lle a elwir 'the place that is called'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a · also softened after the infixed 'th 'you' (na'th elwir 'that you are not called'; ni'th elwir bellach byth yn uorwyn 'you will never again be called a maiden')
weithon: weithon (weithian) — now, at last; adverb, always in this softened form (gweith 'time' + hon 'this'); par weithon wahard 'have (them) forbidden now'
glan: glan (glan) — bank, shore, brink; noun f. (y glan Alaw 'on the bank of the Alaw'); in the text the word is divided y glan, the y standing for yn, whose nasal mutation of glan is not written; the division is an open point
beris: peri (peri) — to cause, make (happen); 3 sg. preterite 'caused' (a beris bot y gaer yma 'who caused the fort to be here'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the relative a
gauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find, reach; 3 sg. preterite 'got', soft-mutated after a (a gauas 'got, reached') · also soft after the particle neur (Neur gauas ef enw 'he has got a name'; neur gauas ef arueu)
cantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', the main administrative division of medieval Wales; noun m. (seith cantref Dyuet 'the seven cantrefs of Dyfed')
kyweiraw: cyweirio (cyweirio) — to prepare, arrange, set in order; verbal noun (a beris kyweiraw lle idaw 'and had a place made ready for him'; eu kyweiraw 'dress them'); no mutation (object/complement of peri, and after eu)
maent: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (y maent yn lluossauc 'they are numerous'); no mutation
awn: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. 'let us go' (Awn parth a'r llys 'let us go towards the court') or 'we will go' (ni a awn)
hedrych: edrych (edrych) — to look, see, look at; verbal noun, with prosthetic h- after y 'her, its' (y hedrych 'to see it', the feminine Dyuet as referent: ac awn y hedrych 'and let us go to see it')
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
aniueileit: aniueil (anifail) — animal, beast; noun m., plural aniueileit (modern anifeiliaid); radical (vowel)
arnunt: ar — conjugated preposition 'on them' (Sef lliw oed arnunt 'this was the colour that was on them')
dala: dala (dal) — to hold, seize, take on; verbal noun (dechreuis gwyr y wlat dala trymuryt 'the men of the land began to take sorrow'); no mutation · also with 'y 'her' before it (a'y dala hi 'and her being caught'; the sense of the clause is a little uncertain)
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
ducpwyt: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; impersonal preterite 'was/were brought' (y ducpwyt gwraged y wylat y mab 'women were brought to watch the boy'), -pwyt the impersonal ending; no mutation after the particle y
kyuodes: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; 3 sg. preterite 'rose' (gyt ac y kyuodes ef 'as soon as he rose'); radical after particle y
guiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, put on armour, arm; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethant (guiscaw a wnaethant wynteu 'they armed themselves'); radical (gu- = gw-)
dodes: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 3 sg. preterite 'put' (a dodes hut ar y wlat 'who put an enchantment on the land'); after the relative a, where d>dd would be unseen in the spelling
gyuodes: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (a gyuodes y uynyd 'and rose up')
uynyd: mynyd (mynydd) — mountain, upward; noun m. used adverbially 'upward', soft-mutated after y (a gyuodes y uynyd 'rose up')
uwrw: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; verbal noun, soft-mutated as possessed object, 'its throwing' = throwing it (yn y uwrw y'r llawr) · also soft after a verb as its object (hi a gynsynwys uwrw neit yn y tan 'she resolved to throw a leap into the fire', i.e. to leap)
uedru: medru (medru) — to hit (a mark), be able; verbal noun, here 'hit', soft-mutated (m>u) after 'y 'its' standing for the object (y uwrw a'y uedru 'throwing at it and hitting it')
ystlys: ystlys (ystlys) — side, edge; noun f. (ystlys y llannerch 'the edge of the clearing')
paladyr: paladyr (paladr) — spear-shaft; noun m. (a'e paladyr 'and his spear')
ohonaw: o + ef — conjugated preposition 'of/by him' (edrych ohonaw ef 'his looking')
bwrw: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast off; verbal noun (bwrw y bratteu 'casting off the rags')
welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as a verbal noun directly after the verb (ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer 'they marvelled to see the fort') · also soft after chawn 'we shall be able' (ni chawn welet 'we shall not be able to see')
odyna: odyna (oddi yna, oddyna) — from there, then, after that; adverb, od 'from' + yna 'there' (Odyna treulaw y ulwydyn 'then spending the year')
maes: maes (maes) — field, open ground; noun m. (o'r maes hwnn 'of this field', of those here)
gyn: kyn (cyn) — as, equative particle before an adjective (kyn hygaret 'as lovable', spelt gyn after ny) · also soft-mutated in a run of epithets after the feminine noun morwyn (morwyn gystal, kyuurd, gyn anwylet 'a maiden so good, of equal rank, so dear') · also soft-mutated after predicative yn (yn gyn hyspysset ganthunt 'as plain to them')
kyrchyssant: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they made for' (y kyrchyssant wynteu Hardlech 'they made for Harlech'; y'r neuad y kyrchyssant 'to the hall they went'); radical after the particle y
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
kyuodi: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; verbal noun (kyuodi a oruc 'he rose')
oruc: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite auxiliary 'he did', soft-mutated after a, with g dropped (kyuodi a oruc)
ardudwy: Proper name — Ardudwy, the cantref in north-west Wales in which Harlech stands; no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
gwledychu: gwledychu (gwladychu) — to rule, reign; verbal noun (gwledychu o honaw 'his ruling')
eidaw: eiddo (eiddo) — that which belongs to someone, 'his'; the independent possessive in 3 sg. m. (yr eidaw ef 'his'; pa darpar oed yr eidaw 'what purpose was his'); no mutation (vowel)
chwedyl: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, report, rumour; noun m. (yd aeth y chwedyl 'the report went'; am y chwedyl 'about the story'); no mutation
trymuryt: trymuryt (trymfryd) — heaviness of mind, sorrow; noun m., trwm 'heavy' + bryt 'mind', b softened inside the compound (dala trymuryt yndunt 'to grow heavy-hearted', literally 'to hold heaviness of mind in them'); no mutation
goueileint: goueileint (no modern form; cf. gofal) — anxiety, care, disquiet; noun (goueileint a dellis yndaw 'anxiety took hold of him'); no mutation
mwy: mwy (mwy) — more, greater; comparative of mawr (mwy yw gan Uendigeituran no chenyt ti 'it is greater to Bendigeidfran than to you'); no mutation (fronted predicate); also mwy dwyweith 'twice as big'
wydyon: Gwydion — personal name (Gwydyon, Wydyon); soft-mutated (G>w) after gan 'with', after e 'to' and in apposition to ynteu (Ynteu Wydyon 'he, Gwydion') · also soft-mutated (G>w) as the subject placed directly after the verb (Val yd oed Wydyon diwarnawt yn y wely 'as Gwydion was in bed one day')
lawer: llawer (llawer) — many, much; pronoun/noun m. (gan lawer o luossogrwyd 'by many of the multitude'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition gan · also adverbial 'by much', softened as an adverb (yn llei lawer no'y throet 'much smaller than her foot')
guydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (also spelt Wydyon, Gwydyon), Math's nephew; Guydyon with u for w; radical (after the particle y in heb y Guydyon 'said Gwydion')
uyth: byth (byth) — ever; with a negative, 'never'; adverb, soft-mutated (b>u) when used adverbially after the verb (dywedy di uyth 'you ever say'; na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'that he may never get me'; a uyd llawn dy got uyth 'will your bag ever be full')
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here · also 'news, tidings' (Pa chwedleu yssyd yma? 'what news is there here?')
nei: nei (nai) — nephew; noun m. (dy nei ditheu 'your nephew too'); no mutation
uo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be', soft-mutated after phan 'when' (phan uo ef ar perued 'when he is in the middle of') · also soft-mutated after the relative a (llathen aryant a uo kyuref 'a rod of silver that may be as thick')
nerth: nerth (nerth) — strength, force; noun m. (o nerth cledyueu 'by force of swords')
yt: y 'to' — conjugated preposition, 2 sg. 'to you', modern iti, spelt yt beside itt and itti (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good'; rac anglot yt 'for fear of dishonour to you'; ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'; derw yt 'it has befallen you') · also yt (ŷd) 'corn, grain', noun m. (yr yt arall 'the other corn')
dechreu: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor 'beginning to muster') · also the noun 'beginning' (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
rodyaw: rodyaw (rhodio) — to walk about, wander, roam; verbal noun in -yaw (wrth rodyaw y wlat 'while roaming the land'); softened after wrth, but r also writes rh, so the change does not show
racdaw: rac (rhag) + ef — conjugated preposition 'before him, on his way' (y kerdaud Arawn racdaw)
gwyned: Gwyned (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales; radical (object of dygyuori; Gwyned a Phowys a Deheubarth)
phowys: Powys — proper name, the kingdom of east and mid Wales; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form · yn y lle 'at once, on the spot' (Ac yn y lle, y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'and at once, as soon as he came to the sea'); lle idaw y benelinyaw 'a place for him to recline' · also 'where' as a relative conjunction with y (lle y gwydat bot gwreic 'where he knew there was a woman')
aruon: Proper name — Arfon, the cantref across the Menai Strait from Môn; no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
maynawr: maenawr (maenor) — manor, a territorial unit; noun f., first element of the names Maynawr Bennard and Maynawr Coet Alun; radical
bennard: Pennard (Pennardd) — proper name; soft-mutated (P>b) after the feminine noun maynawr (Maynawr Bennard 'the manor of Pennard')
diskynnu: diskynnu (disgyn) — to descend, alight; verbal noun (a diskynnu ar e yscwyd 'and alighting on his shoulder')
yno: yno (yno) — there; adverb (ac yno y bu y nos honno)
ymywn: y mywn (mewn) — in, inside; preposition, the old y + mywn (ymywn ty 'inside a house'); no mutation
diwethaf: diwethaf (diwethaf) — last, latest; superlative adjective from diwedd 'end' (y'r grofd diwethaf 'to the last croft'); follows its noun, no mutation
hwch: hwch (hwch) — sow; noun f.; radical (hanner hwch 'half a sow')
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
moch: moch (moch) — pigs; collective plural of mochyn 'pig' (eu moch 'their pigs'); no mutation
ryw: ryw (rhyw) — some, some kind of; before its noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic') · also y ryw wr 'what kind of man'; ryw 'sort, kind' as a noun
gerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, pace; verbal noun/noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y gerdet 'to go'), after vn 'same' (vn gerdet; why is not clear, kerdet being usually masculine), and in amgen urys gerdet 'other haste of pace' (cause unclear) · also soft-mutated after pa 'what' (pa gerdet yssyd arnawch chwi 'what journey is on you?') and after llyna (Llyna gerdet 'there is the journey') · also soft after ar 'on' (ar gerdet 'on the move, walking') · also soft after in 'for us' (reit yw in gerdet 'it is necessary for us to go') · also soft after ywch 'to you' (mi a wnaf ywch gerdet y gyt 'I will make you go together'; verbal noun after the conjugated preposition)
ban: pan (pan) — when; conjunction, spelt ban here (ban uydynt, ban uei 'when they were, when it was'); the b is a spelling of the conjunction, followed by a soft-mutated verb · also hyt ban 'until' (hyt ban gauas y benn 'until he found his head'; o hyn hyt ban del amgen 'from now until something else comes')
creu: creu (modern form uncertain) — sty, pen, enclosure for animals; noun m. (gwneuthur creu y'r moch 'making a sty for the pigs'); radical
beunyd: beunyd (beunydd) — daily, every day; adverb (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw beunyd 'to sit beside it daily'); no mutation
chyn: kyn (cyn) — although, though; spirant-mutated after a (a chyn nyt ymdialwyf 'and though I do not avenge myself') · also the equative particle cyn 'as', spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'and as stout as a boy of six') · also 'before' (a chyn penn y pedwyryd mis 'and before the end of the fourth month')
elei: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'would go' (erbyn pan elei y mab y uarchogaeth 'by the time the boy would go to ride'), -ei; no mutation
nat: na, nat (nad) — 'that … not'; negative conjunction of a subordinate clause, nat before a vowel (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there')
thi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and, with' (gyt a thi 'together with you')
gwnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do' (mi a wnaf hynny 'I will do that')
welas: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. preterite 'saw', soft-mutated after relative y (yny welas y llys a'r kyuanned) · also soft after the particle a (Porth y gaer a welas 'the gate of the fort she saw') and after pan 'when' (Pann welas Kicua 'when Cigfa saw')
lliw: lliw (lliw) — colour; noun m., base unmutated form (Sef lliw oed arnunt)
deffroes: deffroi (deffro) — to wake; 3 sg. preterite 'woke' (Riannon a deffroes 'Rhiannon woke'), -es; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
chyuodi: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (A chyuodi y uynyd 'and rising up')
gwydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (Gwydyon); radical (the y before it in heb y Gwydyon is the particle that introduces a named speaker)
seuyll: seuyll (sefyll) — to stand; verbal noun (yn seuyll yn y lle 'standing at once'); no mutation
hegyr: agori (agor) — to open; 3 sg. present egyr 'opens', used in past narrative for a vivid moment (ual y hegyr 'as he opens it'); the h- marks an infixed object pronoun 'her, it' after the particle y (the chest, kist being feminine); it is not a mutation of the verb
neit: neit (naid) — leap, bound; noun f. (ar yr eil neit 'at the second leap')
cherdet: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a cherdet yn ol y cwn 'and going after the hounds') · also the noun 'pace, gait', spirant-mutated after y 'her' (y cherdet hitheu 'her pace')
braf: praff (praff) — thick, stout, massive; adjective, soft-mutated (p>b) after predicative yn, with f written for ff (yn uawr ac yn braf 'great and stout'; the Red Book yn braff); not modern braf 'fine'
canlynwys: canlyn (canlyn) — to follow; 3 sg. preterite 'followed' (o'r a'm canlynwys i 'of those that have followed me')
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
chyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chyrchu y bordeu 'and making for the tables')
nant: nant (nant) — valley, brook; noun m., first element of the place-name Nant Call; radical
dan: dan (dan) — under; preposition (dan y coet 'under the wood')
prenn: prenn (pren) — tree, wood; noun m. (un prenn 'a single tree'); no mutation
edrychwys: edrych (edrych) — to look; 3 sg. preterite 'he looked' in -wys (A phan edrychwys 'and when he looked'); no mutation (vowel)
beth: beth — what; interrogative pronoun (beth amgen 'what else?', beth a wnaf 'what shall I do?') · also beth ← peth 'thing', softened, in the idiom ys … a beth 'it is a … thing' (ys bychan a beth uyd dy gywilyd 'it is a small thing that your shame will be')
welei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect 'he saw' (welei), soft-mutated after a (ef a welei lannerch) · also 'would see' (neu ynteu a welei rywedawt 'or else he would see a wonder')
kic: kic (cig) — meat, flesh; noun m. (-c = g); object of the verbal noun, no mutation
rei: rei (rhai) — some, some people; pronoun (rei o'r maes hwnn 'some of this field')
mae: bot (bod) — to be; irregular present 3 sg. 'is, there is' (y mae arnat o anryded) · also interrogative 'where is?' (Mae yr yniuer …? 'where is the company …?')
lleu: lleu (lleu) — light, bright, fair; adjective used as a noun with the article, y Lleu 'the fair one' (ys llaw gyffes y medrwys y Lleu ef 'with a steady hand the fair one hit it'), the words that give the boy his name Lleu; ll is not softened after the article
chanu: canu (canu) — to sing, sound; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chanu y gorn 'and sounding his horn')
englyn: englyn (englyn) — an englyn, a short strict-metre verse; noun m. (canu englyn 'to sing a verse')
rwng: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, base uninflected form
deu: deu (dau) — two (m.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following noun (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
awyr: awyr (awyr) — air, sky; noun (yr awyr 'the air'); no mutation (vowel initial)
canu: canu (canu) — to sing, sound (a horn); verbal noun (canu y gorn 'sounding his horn')
uaes: maes (maes) — field; noun m., soft-mutated after o (o uaes guastat 'a level field')
angerd: angerd (angerdd) — fury, ardour, might; noun m.; radical
gyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — apparently 'sure, steady, deft' in Llaw Gyffes 'steady hand' (ys llaw gyffes 'it is with a steady hand'; Llew Llaw Gyffes); whether it is the same word as kyffes 'confession' is uncertain; soft-mutated (k>g) as an adjective after the feminine noun llaw
uyd: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present/future 'is, will be' (byd), soft-mutated after a or a predicate (Dilesteir uyd dy hynt; yny uyd Hafgan)
geing: keing (cainc) — branch, strand, a branch of the Mabinogi; noun f. (y geing hon 'this branch'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article y
trewis: taraw (taro) — to strike; 3 sg. preterite 'he struck' (y trewis ynteu hi a hudlath 'he struck her with a magic wand'); radical after the particle y
hutlath: hudlath (hudlath) — magic wand, enchanter's rod (hud 'magic' + llath 'rod'); noun f. (e hutlath 'the wand'; a'r hutlath 'with the wand'); radical; the sense is disputed (a wand of enchantment vs. a plain staff) and magic wand is likeliest
hunan: hunan (hunan) — self, own; intensive pronoun (e hunan 'himself')
welsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen', soft-mutated after o'r a (o'r a welsei ef) · also soft after the negatives na and ny (hyt na welsei dyn 'so that no man had seen'; ny welsei dyn) · also soft after yr pan 'since' (yr pan welsei ef 'since he had seen')
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
wr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ansyberwyt uwy ar wr) · also soft after y 'to' (y wr 'to a man, to a husband') · also soft in address (A wr 'O man') and after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw wr 'what kind of man') · also subject directly after a negated verb, soft-mutated (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come') · also soft after at 'to' (at wr mawr 'to a great man')
dremynt: tremynt (no modern form; cf. trem 'look') — a sight, spectacle; noun m.; written softened (t>d) with no visible cause: Evans prints no e 'the' before it (the second witness's e dremynt would explain it) (o achaws dremynt 'because of a sight') · also soft-mutated (t>d) after a preceding adjective, the cause there (A fell dremynt oed udunt y guelet 'and a far sight it was for them to see', fell = pell 'far')
ascwrn: ascwrn (asgwrn) — bone; noun m. (wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone'); no mutation (vowel)
caer: caer (caer) — fortress, walled court; noun f.; first element of the place-name Caer Tathyl, Math's court (Caer Dathyl); radical as object after a gyrchwys
gahat: caffael (cael) — to get; impersonal preterite 'was got' (Sef a gahat yn y kynghor 'what was got in the counsel'), kahat; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
wrthaw: wrth (wrth) + ef — conjugated preposition 'to/at him' (a dywedut ual hynn wrthaw) · also in y wrthaw, e wrthaw 'from him, away from him'
kyn: kyn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun (kyn uy rodi 'before my being given') · also the equative particle 'as', softening the adjective (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy') · also 'although', with the subjunctive (Kyn ny bwyf arglwydes 'though I am not a lady') · also in kyn no hynny 'before that' (seith mlyned kyn no hynny 'seven years before that')
kyuyl: cyfyl (cyfyl) — neighbourhood, vicinity, presence; noun m. (yng kyuyl y llys 'in the vicinity of the court'); written radical, the nasal mutation after yng being shown on the preposition only
holl: holl (holl) — all, whole; adjective, precedes its noun causing soft mutation (yr holl gyuoeth 'the whole realm')
madws: madws — a word of uncertain origin and exact force, generally taken as 'it is time, it is fitting'; predicate with oed (madws oed ymi cael attep 'it was time for me to get an answer')
caffael: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain, win; verbal noun (caffael o honot 'your getting/winning')
iawn: iawn — right, proper, correct; adjective/predicate (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also noun 'compensation, redress, amends' (dy iawn 'your compensation'; chael iawn 'getting redress') · also 'right (thing)' as object of gwneuthur (phei gwnelut iawn 'and if you were to do right')
keueis: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 1 sg. preterite 'I got' (y keueis wynt 'I had them'); no mutation after the particle y
ouut: gofut (gofid) — grief, trouble, distress; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (o ouut 'of grief')
eill: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. present, irregular form 'may, can' (ef a eill uot 'it may be')
goreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good' (Goreu yw gennyf 'it is best with me' = I prefer)
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation · also y genhyf 'from me' (yny caffo y genhyf i 'until he gets it from me'), with y 'from' (y gan)
bo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be' (Vrth ual y bo dy anryded 'according as your rank may be')
kyntaf: kyntaf (cyntaf) — first; superlative of kynt, used adverbially and adjectivally
dygyuoryaw: dygyuoryaw (no distinct modern form; cf. dygyfor 'muster') — to muster, gather; verbal noun (y dygyuoryaw yr ynys honn y gyt 'to muster this island together')
mur: mur (mur) — wall; noun m., first part of the place-name Mur Castell, where Lleu's court was set (the Red Book Mur y Castell); radical
castell: castell (castell) — castle, fort; noun m., second part of the place-name Mur Castell (the Red Book Mur y Castell); radical
clybot: clybot (clywed) — to hear; verbal noun (guedy clybot dy uot yn kyuanhedu 'after hearing that you were settling'); radical after guedy
kymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun (iawn yw gymryt; kymryt gwrogaeth)
morynyon: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden, girl; plural morynyon (modern morynion); radical after the article y with a plural
mynyd: mynyd (mynydd) — mountain; noun m. (mynyd mawr 'a great mountain'); no mutation
thrwy: trwy (trwy) — through, by; preposition, spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and' (a thrwy gynghor Branuen 'and by the counsel of Branwen')
ouyn: ofyn (ofn) — fear; noun m., u for the v-sound (nyt oes arnaf i ouyn 'I have no fear', literally 'there is no fear on me') · also 3 sg. present of gouyn (gofyn) 'asks', with g lost by soft mutation after a (ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'); a different word from ofyn 'fear' · also 2 sg. imperative of gouyn (gofyn) 'ask', g lost by soft mutation after na (na ouyn di yni y mab 'do not ask us for the boy') · also verbal noun gouyn 'asking', g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ouyn 'without asking') and after y 'to' (y ouyn idaw 'to ask of him')
hwyneb: wyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., with h- after y 'her' (am y hwyneb 'about her face')
tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud) · also 'beyond', preposition (tra y gefyn 'beyond his back', i.e. back again)
keuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m. (wrth y keuyn 'at the back'); no mutation
wybuant: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 pl. preterite 'they knew' in -uant (hyt na wybuant wy eiryoet 'so that they never knew'); g- lost by soft mutation after na
llyn: llyn (llyn) — lake, pool; noun m. (uch penn llyn 'above a lake'; Llyn y Peir 'the Lake of the Cauldron') · also 'drink, liquor' (o uwyt a llyn 'of food and drink'); no mutation
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
ladaf: llad (lladd) — to kill; 1 sg. present/future 'I will kill' (ni ladaf i di)
wnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do', soft-mutated after a (mi a wnaf hynny) · also 'I will see to it, bring it about that' (mi a wnaf na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'I will see that he never gets me'); auxiliary (Y gymryt a wnaf 'I will take it')
waeth: gwaeth (gwaeth) — worse; comparative (kyrch waeth 'a worse journey'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the noun kyrch it follows
ellwng: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; verbal noun (ellwng e gwn 'to loose his hounds') · also 2 sg. imperative 'release!' (Ellwng ef 'Release it')
ederyn: ederyn (aderyn) — bird; noun m.; object of the verbal noun meithryn, no mutation (vowel)
kywilyd: cywilydd (cywilydd) — shame, disgrace; noun m. (Vyg kywilyd 'my shame', object fronted); written radical, the nasal mutation shown only in vyg
wnaethost: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. preterite 'you did', soft-mutated after a (A wnaethost, heb ef, yrof i)
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him') · also 'not' in a main-clause denial or refusal, with soft mutation (na ellynghaf 'I will not release'; na uynhaf 'I will not have it'; na weleis 'I have not seen')
dangos: dangos (dangos) — to show, make known; verbal noun (y erchi … dangos 'to bid (them) show themselves')
wyneb: gwyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., base unmutated form
byth: byth (byth) — ever, for ever; adverb (Nyt byth y perhey di 'you will not last for ever'); no mutation
adar: aderyn (aderyn) — bird; plural adar 'birds'; in the title Adar Riannon 'the Birds of Rhiannon', the plural noun followed by a name in the genitive; radical
anyan: anian (anian) — nature, disposition, kind; noun f.; radical (ac yn un anyan a'r gwyduilot 'and of one nature with the wild beasts'; a'r anyan a uo y'r moch coet 'and the nature that belongs to the wild swine'); a- vowel, no mutation
udunt: y (i) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'to them' (Amser a doeth udunt e uynet e gyscu)
enw: enw (enw) — name; noun m. (y enw ef 'his name')
alw: galw (galw) — to call; verbal noun, g lost by soft mutation after y 'his' standing for the object (a'y alw attaw 'and he called him to him')
ieith: ieith (iaith) — language, speech; noun f. (dyscu ieith 'teaching speech'); no mutation
etwa: etwa (eto) — yet, still; adverb (nys mynnaf etwa 'I do not want him yet')
gyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after y (y gyrchwys 'he made for') · also soft-mutated after the relative particle a with the object fronted (y gaer a gyrchwys ef 'the fort he made for') · also soft after a with the subject fronted (Enteu Math a gyrchwys Caer Tathyl 'and Math made for Caer Dathyl'; y mor a gyrchwys 'he made for the sea')
odyno: odyno (oddi yno) — from there, thence; adverb, o 'from' + yno 'there' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there')
kennadwri: kennadwri (cenhadwri) — message, embassy, errand; noun f. (am ych kennadwri chwi 'about your message')
uynnei: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after relative a (a uynnei y hela)
tir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m. (dylyedauc tir a dayar 'a lord of land and earth')
dayar: dayar (daear) — earth, land; noun f. (am dir a dayar 'about land and earth')
aryant: aryant (arian) — silver, money; noun m. (llathen aryant 'a rod of silver'); no mutation (vowel)
chymeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. present/future 'I will take' (ny chymeraf i 'I will not take'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ny
dygaf: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. present 'I bring' (y dygaf uy nghyffes 'I bring my confession')
uyg: uy (fy) — my; possessive, here spelt uyg before k-: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation the noun would take (uyg kyuoeth = fy nghyfoeth 'my realm')
