kyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession; noun f. (ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God'; the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); ym is taken as 'my', and the nasal mutation it brings (nghyffes) is not shown in the spelling
peth: peth (peth) — thing; noun m., used with bynnac 'whatever' (Peth bynnac o garueidrwyd)
gymeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. present/future 'I will take' (mi a'th gymeraf yn wreic im 'I will take you as wife'; hwnn a gymeraf i 'this one I will take'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the infixed 'th 'you' and after the relative a with the object fronted
oedwn: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. imperfect 'I was' (yd oedwn inheu)
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
gadel: gadel (gadael) — to leave, let; verbal noun (gadel y uarch … y gerdet 'letting his horse go')
dir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m., soft-mutated after am (am dir a dayar 'about land and earth')
gwyrda: gwyrda (gwŷr da) — noblemen; gwyr 'men' + da 'good' (Vy ngwyrda 'my noblemen', nasal-mutated after uy)
kywir: kywir (cywir) — faithful, true; adjective (Vy ngwyrda kywir 'my faithful noblemen')
teulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband, a lord's retinue; noun m. (later came to mean 'family')
maeth: maeth (maeth) — fostering, nurture, fosterage; noun m., in mab maeth 'foster-son' (mab maeth ynni uyd 'he will be a foster-son to us'); no mutation
ohonawch: o (o) — of, from; 2 pl. conjugated form 'of you' (a oes ohonawch i 'is there (any) of you'); the following i is probably the echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending
chwi: chwi (chi) — 'you' (pl.); pronoun (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you')
drossof: tros (tros) — for, on behalf of; conjugated preposition 'for me' (1 sg.) (drossof 'on my behalf')
nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything') · also Nac ef 'no', literally 'not it', refusing a proposal (Nac ef, heb y Manawydan 'No, said Manawydan')
wynt: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; 3 pl. pronoun (un lliw ac wynt 'the same colour as them') · also Wynt, Gwent, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed', a region of south-east Wales
dros: dros (dros) — over, across; preposition (dros pedrein y uarch 'over the crupper of his horse') · also 'for, instead of' before a verbal noun, which it softens (dros wneuthur 'instead of doing'; the sense there is not certain)
harglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m. (a'e harglwyd 'and their lord'); h- prefixed to the vowel after the possessive e/eu 'their'
gelwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (Ac y gelwir y rei hynny 'and those are called'), -ir, a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle y
hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast' · also 'so that' with the indicative (hyt nat oed rym 'so that there was no use'); hyt yn Aberfraw 'as far as Aberffraw' · also the noun 'length, duration' after pa 'what' (Pa hyt bynnac y bydynt ar y ford 'however long they were on the road')
trydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ar y trydyd 'at the third') · also in the triad formula, 'the third (of three)', one of a set of three (A hwnnw a uu trydyd anuat ergyt 'and that was one of the three ill-fated blows')
deulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y deulu 'and his warband') · also deu lu 'two hosts' written as one word (y deulu 'the two hosts'; the Red Book writes y deulu where the White Book has y deu lu)
kymeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. present 'I take, I shall take' (ys kymeraf gynghor 'I shall take counsel')
yll: yll (ill) — the pronoun used before a numeral, 'they (all)': y rydunt yll pymp 'between them, the five of them' (modern ill dau 'the two of them'); no mutation
llew: Llew (Lleu) — personal name, a spelling of Lleu (Llew Llaw Gyffes yw bellach 'Lleu Llaw Gyffes he is henceforth'); w is the 6-shaped w here; radical
gwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., meaning as context decides (a'y wreic 'and his wife')
gwneuthum: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. preterite 'I did' (a wneuthum i yrot ti 'what I did for you')
wneuthum: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. preterite 'I did', soft-mutated after a/o (gwneuthur a wneuthum itt)
archaf: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 1 sg. present 'I ask'; the stem vowel is a (arch-), which becomes e in erchi (nyt archaf 'I do not ask'; Sef arch a archaf 'the request I ask')
llech: llech (llech) — flat stone, slab; noun f.; no mutation (uch benn llech 'above a slab'; wrth y llech 'to the slab')
welaf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present 'I see', soft-mutated after a (mi a welaf 'I see')
dyrnawt: dyrnawt (dyrnod) — a blow; variant spelling of dyrnaut (angheuawl dyrnawt 'a deadly blow')
ryngtaw: rwng (rhwng) + ef — 'between him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., used in the idiom ryngtaw a 'between him and' = on his way to (Ef a aeth ryngtaw a llys Eueyd Hen 'he went his way to the court of Heueyd the Old') · also in its plain sense 'between him (and)' (gadu y ryngtaw ef a Guydyon 'leave it between him and Gwydion')
drwydi: trwy (trwy) — through; conjugated preposition 3 sg. f. 'through it' (the river is feminine) (ny eill neb uynet drwydi 'no one can go through it'); MW often writes the preposition with d- (drwy) where no mutation is due, as drwy Linon
dyrr: torri (torri) — to break; 3 sg. present, vivid narrative tense 'breaks' (yny dyrr yr arueu oll 'so that all the armour breaks')
llas: lladd (lladd) — to strike, kill, cut off; 3 sg. impersonal/passive preterite 'was struck, was cut' (y llas y benn ef 'his head was struck off'); radical after the particle y
ettwa: ettwa (etwa, eto) — still, yet; adverb (nyt hir ettwa yd ym y gyt 'it is not long yet that we are together'); no mutation
eilweith: eilweith (eilwaith) — a second time, again; adverb, eil 'second' + gweith 'time', gweith softened (gw>w) after eil inside the compound; no mutation of the whole word
gwledychwys: gwledychu (gwledychu) — to rule, reign; 3 sg. preterite 'ruled' (Ac y gwledychwys ynteu Pryderi seith cantref Dyuet 'and Pryderi ruled the seven cantrefs of Dyfed'), -wys; no mutation after the particle y
herwyd: herwyd (herwydd) — in respect of, according to; preposition (yn herwyd ymlad 'in respect of fighting')
dyweit: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. present 'says' (guir a dyweit 'he tells the truth'); modern dywed
kyuarwydyt: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, story, storytelling (the old sense; the modern word means 'guidance'); noun m. (y kyuarwydyt hwnnw 'that tale'); radical after the article
wyned: Gwyned (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales; soft-mutated (Gw>w) after ar 'over' (arglwyd ar Wyned 'lord over Gwynedd')
teruyna: terfynu (terfynu) — to end, finish; 3 sg. present 'ends' (y teruyna y geing hon yma 'this branch ends here'); no mutation after the particle y
mabinogi: mabinogi (mabinogi) — the Mabinogi; noun m., here the title in Mabinogi Mynweir a Mynord; the original meaning (tale of youth?) is disputed; radical
